title: Understanding Traffic Flow for VPN (For Legacy Apps) Log Fields

blocks.text: The Log Streaming Service (LSS) can send Traffic Flow VPN log information to any third-party log analytics tool. By default, the Traffic Flow VPN log type includes the fields listed in the following table for each log template (i.e., CSV, JSON, TSV). While configuring your log receiver, you can edit the default log stream content to capture only specific fields, and create a custom log template.

blocks.item: View a Traffic Flow log fields example.

blocks.text: The following table includes descriptions and supported field format specifications for each field within the template. To learn more about the format specifications listed for each field, including examples, see Understanding the Log Stream Content Format.

table: The timestamp when the log was generated
The unique ID assigned to traffic flow
The unique identifier for the user connection
The state of the traffic flow session (e.g., open or closed)
The VPN Service Edge used for the traffic
The Common Name component of the SSL/TLS certificate for identifying the primary identity
The username entered in Zscaler Client Connector
The name of the device reported by Zscaler Client Connector. This field only provides valid values for Zscaler Client Connector and machine tunnel client types.
The L4 protocol number per IANA standards
The source IP address used in the connection
The source port used in the connection
The destination IP address used in the connection
The destination port used in the connection
The time when the traffic flow started
The time when the traffic flow ended
The total bytes of data received during the session
The total bytes of data sent during the session
The number of data packets received during the session
The number of data packets sent during the session
